original_question: In dimensions n >= 3, is the sum of the relative frequencies of all possible faces finite?
target_in_paper: Section 3.4, Problem 17 ("Is that true that sum of all relative frequencies for all possible faces is finite for higher dimensions?")
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the exact finiteness issue posed in the paper and correctly places it in the higher-dimensional regime n >= 3. It is very close in substance to Problem 17 in Section 3.4.
missing_details: The question is about faces of sails of geometric n-dimensional continued fractions, not arbitrary polyhedral faces.
The ambient setting is the real space with its integer lattice, as in the paper's setup for geometric multidimensional continued fractions and sails.

The phrase "relative frequencies" refers to the Möbius-geometric relative frequencies discussed in Section 3.4, i.e. frequencies coming from the projectively invariant Möbius measure on the space of arrangements.

To make the summation mathematically meaningful and faithful to the nearby formulation in Problem 16, the sum should be understood over possible face types up to integer congruence (equivalently, over pairwise integer non-congruent possible faces).
It should be explicit that the quantifier is fixed-dimension: for each dimension n >= 3, ask whether that total sum is finite.
It should be explicit that "all possible faces" means all face types that can actually occur as faces of n-dimensional continued fractions/sails in the paper's sense.
The question belongs specifically to the sail-statistics / generalized Gauss-Kuzmin part of the paper, not to the face-classification or torus-decomposition problems.
refined_question: For each dimension n >= 3, in the sail-statistics setting of geometric n-dimensional continued fractions (sails with respect to the integer lattice), where relative frequencies are defined via the Möbius-invariant measure on the space of arrangements, is the sum of the relative frequencies over all possible face types that occur in such n-dimensional continued fractions, counted up to integer congruence, finite?
justification: The draft is essentially a near-verbatim paraphrase of Problem 17 in Section 3.4. The only paper-faithful sharpening needed is to restore the omitted context: the paper is speaking about faces of sails of geometric multidimensional continued fractions; the relevant frequencies are the Möbius-measure-based relative frequencies described immediately before Problems 15-18; and the nearby Problem 16 shows that the natural counting is by pairwise integer non-congruent face types. Section 3.1 confirms that this is part of the generalized Gauss-Kuzmin face-distribution program for sails.
